name: Rishiganga–Dhauliganga–Alaknanda flood, 7 Feb 2021 (Chamoli)

historical.note: The real 7 Feb 2021 disaster was a rock–ice avalanche from Ronti peak (~27 million m³, Shugar et al. 2021) that turned into a debris flow down the Rishiganga and Dhauliganga. This scenario does NOT reproduce that mechanism: it reconstructs the event as a clear-water outburst from an illustrative blockage in the Rishiganga gorge upstream of Raini, holding a comparable volume. Treat it as a hindcast-style what-if for the flood path, not a reconstruction of the debris flow.

summary: Illustrative ~27 million m³ water outburst from a blockage in the Rishiganga gorge above Raini, routed over real SRTM terrain past Raini, Tapovan, Joshimath, Helang and Pipalkoti to Chamoli.

dem.source: AWS Open Data Terrain Tiles, Terrarium encoding, zoom 13 (https://s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png); SRTM-derived in this region; box-filter area-averaged to 60 m cells
dem.conditioning: 0 void cells filled; 794 single-cell pits raised to their lowest neighbour (mean 2.7 m, max 26.0 m); minimal-change (L1 isotonic) strictly-descending fit along the traced river path: 512 of 896 river-path cells changed by >0.5 m (261 raised, 251 lowered; median |dz| 6.4 m; 165 cells >10 m; max raise 60.1 m, max lowering 61.2 m)

dam.name: Illustrative Rishiganga gorge blockage
dam.type: Illustrative natural blockage (debris/ice dam) — not a real structure
dam.publishedVolumeSource: Shugar et al. (2021), Science 373:300-306 — ~27×10⁶ m³ rock–ice avalanche volume of the real event; used only as the target volume for this illustrative water blockage (no real lake of this size existed).

stageStorage.note: Integrated on a 30 m grid resampled from Terrarium z13 tiles over [79.66, 30.38, 79.95, 30.56]: cells hydraulically connected to the reservoir below each level without crossing the dam line (minimax priority flood), volume = Σ(level − ground)·cell area. Crest elevation 2400 m was chosen so the DEM table holds ≈27 million m³ (illustrative). Table extends 10 m above the crest assuming closed valley sides. At the initial level the reservoir spans [79.722, 30.463, 79.737, 30.471], entirely inside the simulation box.

breach.note: Froehlich (2008) regression: Bavg = 0.27·k0·Vw^0.32·Hb^0.04 = 104 m, tf = 63.2·√(Vw/(g·Hb²)) = 9.0 min, with k0 = 1.3 (overtopping (lake assumed full to the crest)), Vw = 27.1 million m³ (DEM table, initial level 2400 m above breach bottom), Hb = 193.7 m (crest − SRTM bed). finalWidth is the bottom width Bavg − z·Hb; Froehlich's side slope would give a bottom width below half the average width, so the side slope was reduced to 0.27 (H:V) to keep bottom width = Bavg/2 while preserving the regression's average width. Hb and/or Vw are beyond the range of Froehlich's calibration data, so treat these as order-of-magnitude defaults.

notes: The blockage location, height and volume are ILLUSTRATIVE. The site is the narrowest 60 m-grid cross-section of the Rishiganga between ~0.8 km above Raini and the Ronti Gad confluence; the crest height is whatever the DEM stage-storage needs to hold ~27 million m³ there.

The real 2021 flow was a sediment-laden debris flow with far higher density and bulking than clear water; peak stages and travel times from a clear-water shallow-water model will differ from the observed event.
Dam axis location: narrowest of 62 main-stem cells on OSM way 1074462194 0.8–4.5 km from the reference confluence (80 m above bed: 210 m wide).

Elevation is SRTM-derived (Feb 2000) surface elevation area-averaged to 60 m: no river bathymetry, and channels narrower than a cell are not resolved (valley floors are biased high where the gorge is narrower than 60 m).

DEM conditioning: 0 void cells filled; 794 single-cell pits raised to their lowest neighbour (mean 2.7 m, max 26.0 m); minimal-change (L1 isotonic) strictly-descending fit along the traced river path: 512 of 896 river-path cells changed by >0.5 m (261 raised, 251 lowered; median |dz| 6.4 m; 165 cells >10 m; max raise 60.1 m, max lowering 61.2 m).
Stage-storage is DEM-integrated (see stageStorage.note); no published reservoir volume exists for this illustrative blockage.
DamSpec.height = crest 2400 m − lowest SRTM bed within 120 m downstream of the axis (2206.3 m).
Default duration = river path length 63.4 km at an assumed 3 m/s mean front speed, rounded up to whole hours (heuristic, not a prediction).

Populations: OSM population tag where present, otherwise a typical value for the place type (city 100,000, town 10,000, village 1,000, hamlet 150), flagged populationSource "typical" — not a census figure.
basinHandoff: the traced path leaves the box at the outlet point; the flood continues in basin reach alaknanda_2 of data/ganga/rivers.json.
